properties.name: Presentation Transformation Platform
properties.description: Define an unwanted visual experience, learn its desired replacement from controlled examples, and apply a reusable policy inside the application's production process. Reference slice: blood becomes glitter in a controlled Linux/Vulkan-backed game. This is a build specification, not evidence that the platform has been implemented.

properties.name: Architecture governance
properties.description: Owns cross-system modeling and substitution conformance. This is a governance role, not a fifth independently realizable system.

properties.name: Domain · Meaning
properties.description: Defines concepts, behavior, relationships and invariants independently of systems and technology.

properties.name: Systems · Responsibility
properties.description: Assigns responsibilities and behavioral contracts independently of implementation mechanisms.

properties.name: Realization · Mechanism
properties.description: Describes boundaries, capabilities and bindings without redefining system identity.

properties.name: Experience
properties.description: An evolving state influenced by inputs and time.

properties.name: Representation
properties.description: Information describing some aspect of an experience.

properties.name: Production
properties.description: A process consuming and producing representations; it may be a graph, not a linear pipeline.

properties.name: Presentation
properties.description: The perceptible result of production.

properties.name: Objective
properties.description: A desired change to an experience.

properties.name: Intervention
properties.description: A controlled modification to representation or production.

properties.name: Counterfactual
properties.description: An alternative outcome originating from equivalent controlled conditions.

properties.name: Evidence
properties.description: Observations with provenance supporting an inference or evaluation.

properties.name: Policy
properties.description: A reusable rule governing interventions.

properties.name: D1 · Causal correspondence
properties.description: Controlled alternatives share identifiable originating conditions.

properties.name: D2 · Provenance
properties.description: Evidence identifies its source and observation boundary.

properties.name: D3 · Preservation
properties.description: Interventions preserve properties not authorized for modification.

properties.name: D4 · Presentation protection
properties.description: No prohibited presentation is allowed in covered production scenarios when strict prevention is promised. Research capture of an original variant is distinct from protected production presentation.

properties.name: D5 · Performance
properties.description: Runtime execution satisfies its declared latency and throughput budget.

properties.name: D6 · Reproducibility
properties.description: Experimental outcomes can be reproduced within declared tolerances.

properties.name: D7 · Semantic stability
properties.description: Representation and implementation changes do not silently redefine objectives.

properties.name: S1 · Counterfactual Experimentation · Research / capture
properties.description: Research / capture

properties.name: Counterfactual Experimentation responsibility
properties.description: Generate comparable experiences and capture their native representations.

properties.name: S1 · Behavioral contract
properties.description: Attributable counterfactual evidence
statements: Reproduce or align equivalent originating states.
Apply declared differences between variants.
Capture available representations at specified observation boundaries.
Preserve native representation data and necessary references.
Record correspondence and provenance.
Make experimental outcomes independently verifiable.
Parallel rendering branches and sequential deterministic replay are alternatives, not mandatory mechanisms.
Boundary: produces evidence; does not own interpretation, policy learning or runtime execution.

properties.name: S2 · Transformation Synthesis · Offline synthesis
properties.description: Offline synthesis

properties.name: Transformation Synthesis responsibility
properties.description: Turn objectives and experimental evidence into reusable, validated interventions.

properties.name: S2 · Behavioral contract
properties.description: Policies with applicability and validation evidence
statements: Consume evidence without assuming a particular engine or graphics API.
Identify or synthesize candidate transformations.
Evaluate desired effects, preservation and cost.
Describe capabilities needed to execute a candidate.
Publish versioned policies with explicit applicability and validation evidence.
Deterministic analysis, statistical learning, neural models and search are replaceable synthesis methods.
Boundary: produces intervention knowledge; does not own environmental execution.

properties.name: S3 · Presentation Mediation · Production runtime
properties.description: Production runtime

properties.name: Presentation Mediation responsibility
properties.description: Apply policies within supported production environments without violating constraints.

properties.name: S3 · Behavioral contract
properties.description: Modified presentation within declared constraints
statements: Identify target capabilities and determine whether a policy can be validly executed.
Prepare transformations before the critical rendering path whenever possible.
Execute through the cheapest suitable interaction boundary.
Enforce required presentation and performance constraints.
Report unsupported policies rather than claiming weaker guarantees.
Expose execution evidence for evaluation and feedback.
Boundary: executes interventions; does not own user objectives or policy learning.

properties.name: S4 · Preference Management · User intent and feedback
properties.description: User intent and feedback

properties.name: Preference Management responsibility
properties.description: Express desired changes and collect feedback independently of execution mechanisms.

properties.name: S4 · Behavioral contract
properties.description: Technology-independent objectives
statements: Allow users to identify an undesirable experience or region and express the intended outcome.
Associate preferences with scope.
Record corrections and observed failures.
Request activation of compatible policies.
Users need not understand shaders, graphics APIs, rendering buffers or model architectures.

properties.name: Evaluation

properties.name: Applicability

properties.name: Presentation Target

properties.name: Policy Binding

properties.name: Installation

properties.name: Execution

properties.name: Interaction Boundary

properties.name: Capability

properties.name: Abstraction Layer
properties.description: Classification of a boundary by available information and operations; not a mandatory pipeline stage.

properties.name: Binding

properties.name: C1 · Transformation Objective
properties.description: Portable meaning of the requested change.
statements: Target concept or behavior; desired outcome; applicability scope.
Preservation requirements; performance constraints; protection requirements.

properties.name: C2 · Counterfactual Evidence
properties.description: Causally aligned native observations and outcomes.
statements: Shared originating conditions; controlled variants; declared interventions.
Observation boundaries; native representation references; correspondence and provenance; observed outcomes.
Observation boundaries identify the stage and interpretation of referenced data.
Commands must include or reference required resource and execution state for supported analysis or replay.

properties.name: C3 · Transformation Policy
properties.description: Portable intent and validity; executable realizations may be platform-specific.
statements: Policy identity and version; objective; applicability conditions.
Required capabilities; executable realizations; evaluation evidence.
Preservation and performance constraints.

properties.name: C4 · Execution Outcome
properties.description: Execution observations, supported status and attributable failures.
statements: Executed policy and target; supported or unsupported status; observed modification.
Preservation results; frame-time and latency measurements; failures and unsupported capabilities.

properties.name: C5 · Capability Description
properties.description: Discoverable capabilities, not assumptions based on a technology name.
statements: Available observation and control boundaries; supported abstraction layers.
Representation formats; execution constraints; timing or presentation guarantees.

properties.name: L1 · State / Semantics
properties.description: Entities, behavior and events; candidate boundaries include engine state and application models.

properties.name: L2 · Presentation Description
properties.description: Layout, geometry, materials and visual properties; candidate boundaries include scene graphs and UI layout.

properties.name: L3 · Rendering Operations
properties.description: Draw commands, shaders, resources and buffers; candidate boundaries include Vulkan, Direct3D and rendering backends.

properties.name: L4 · Composed Representation
properties.description: Completed surfaces and pixels; candidate boundaries include compositors and frame buffers.

properties.name: L5 · Physical Presentation
properties.description: Scanout, hardware composition and timing; candidate boundaries include DRM/KMS and display controllers.

properties.name: Controlled Linux / Godot environment
properties.description: Proposed Godot 4 scene on a Linux desktop with a Vulkan-capable GPU and 120 Hz presentation target. Exact hardware, driver, workload and tolerances must be pinned before acceptance measurements.

properties.name: Engine state and scene boundary
properties.description: Proposed control of scenario state, events, camera, materials and effects.

properties.name: Vulkan operation/resource boundary
properties.description: Proposed capture and intervention boundary. Specificity, resource completeness and timing support require evidence.

properties.name: Offline native-evidence analysis boundary
properties.description: Reads explicitly typed native representations and their interpretation metadata; no universal intermediate representation is required.

properties.name: Local preference interaction boundary
properties.description: Proposed user selection, objective and correction interface. User meaning remains independent of graphics representation.

properties.name: Compositor boundary
properties.description: Replaceable candidate observing composed pixels; semantic identity and pre-exposure guarantees must not be assumed.

properties.name: Controlled state and replay
properties.description: Reproduce or align simulation states, inputs, logical time, event identity and camera within declared tolerances.

properties.name: Native capture with resource closure
properties.description: Capture commands, resources, shaders and relevant execution state at identified boundaries, retaining necessary references.

properties.name: Causal correspondence
properties.description: Relate operations and observations to shared originating conditions and controlled differences.

properties.name: Native transformation analysis
properties.description: Interpret native evidence sufficiently to derive candidate changes and validate their applicability.

properties.name: Specific effect targeting
properties.description: Identify the intended semantic target through available observations with enough specificity to preserve unrelated content.

properties.name: Prepared intervention
properties.description: Prepare and apply an authorized intervention at a supported boundary while preserving the applicable contract and invariants.

properties.name: Covered pre-exposure protection
properties.description: Prevent prohibited production presentation in covered scenarios, or report unsupported unless an explicit conservative mode is authorized.

properties.name: Separated timing and outcome measurement
properties.description: Measure presentation, GPU execution, CPU submission, input-to-display latency and preservation without confusing offline capture cost with runtime cost.

properties.name: Selection and correction
properties.description: Associate a selected region with its observation, express an outcome and scope, request activation and record corrections.

properties.name: S1 · Controlled experiment binding
properties.description: Godot simulation with Vulkan capture/replay is proposed. Unreal, custom simulation and browser automation are alternatives only where sufficient capabilities are demonstrated.

properties.name: S2 · Offline synthesis binding
properties.description: Initial deterministic analysis may derive changed resource/shader relationships from paired records; learned synthesis, program synthesis and rule inference may fulfill the same contract.

properties.name: S3 · Graphics intervention binding
properties.description: Proposed Vulkan interception and resource/shader substitution. Engine integration, other graphics APIs and compositor integration require separate conformance evaluation.

properties.name: S4 · Local preference binding
properties.description: Proposed local preference UI with region selection; desktop overlays, mobile applications and other UIs may implement the same responsibility.

properties.name: Godot
properties.description: Reuse interactive simulation; do not build a rendering engine.

properties.name: Vulkan
properties.description: Reuse graphics API; suitability depends on observed capabilities, not the technology name.

properties.name: GFXReconstruct
properties.description: Candidate graphics capture/replay tooling; verify capture completeness and replay support for the selected scene.

properties.name: RenderDoc
properties.description: Candidate rendering inspection and pixel provenance diagnostics; inspection is separate from production runtime.

properties.name: Existing Vulkan / SPIR-V tooling
properties.description: Reuse shader compilation and inspection tooling; no custom compiler is required.

properties.name: Mesa or supported vendor driver
properties.description: Reuse an existing Linux graphics driver; shader replacement mechanisms are candidates where sufficient.

properties.name: Existing graphics interception mechanisms
properties.description: Extend only where capabilities are insufficient; never circumvent protected content or anti-cheat.

properties.name: Existing analysis and learning infrastructure
properties.description: Prefer reuse for model architecture and training where compatible with native evidence and contracts.

properties.name: P1 · Paired comparable observations
properties.description: Produce paired observations of equivalent experiences.

properties.name: P2 · Native pre-presentation evidence
properties.description: Capture native pre-presentation representations, not only images.

properties.name: P3 · Reusable learned transformations
properties.description: Derive reusable transformation policies from paired evidence.

properties.name: P4 · Single runtime production path
properties.description: Execute a policy without rendering the entire experience twice.

properties.name: P5 · Real-time performance
properties.description: Preserve performance of real-time applications within declared budgets.

properties.name: P6 · Technology-independent meaning
properties.description: Keep domain and system ontologies independent of technology.

properties.name: P7 · User-defined transformation
properties.description: Allow users to define and correct desired transformations.

properties.name: P8 · Replaceable bindings
properties.description: Support different environment bindings without redefining system contracts.

properties.name: P9 · Broader applications and mobile
properties.description: Extend to arbitrary applications and mobile operating systems without assuming equivalent capabilities.

properties.description: Derive and evaluate candidate transformation policies.

properties.description: Publish policies with capability and applicability requirements.

properties.name: F08 · Capability discovery

properties.name: F09 · Prepared compatible transformation
properties.description: Prepare and install compatible transformations.

properties.name: Reference · Blood becomes glitter
properties.description: A controlled Godot 4 scene on Linux with Vulkan-backed rendering and a 120 Hz presentation target. One authoritative simulation establishes equivalent originating conditions. Original and modified variants may be produced by branches or deterministic replay; equivalence must be verified.
statements: Original: scripted action produces blood; native rendering state and output are recorded for evaluation.
Modified: equivalent state, inputs, timing and camera produce glitter; capture occurs at the same logical boundary.
Preserve logical time, event identity, shaders/resources/state, known intervention, correspondence and presentation outcomes.
Images verify results; upstream native representations are the training/analysis evidence.

properties.name: Replace blood with glitter
properties.description: Change visible blood into glitter in the supported reference experience while preserving unrelated scene properties and the declared protection and performance constraints.

properties.name: 1 · Capture controlled alternatives
properties.description: Scenario → controlled variants → observations → attributed counterfactual evidence. Capture native payload and resource closure; verify originating-state equivalence and presentation correspondence.

properties.name: 2 · Derive and evaluate policy
properties.description: Objective and paired evidence produce a candidate intervention. Initially deterministic analysis may derive the changed shader/resource relationship. Validate by replay or equivalent controlled execution before publication.

properties.name: Production · Execute in the normal path
properties.description: Launch the reference game in its original configuration. Discover compatible capabilities, prepare the policy, and substitute matching operations/resources so covered runtime presentation is modified.

properties.name: Feedback · Inspect execution and correct
properties.description: User inspects the observed execution outcome and gives corrections if behavior is wrong.

properties.name: User expression · Select and request
properties.description: Select or circle unwanted content on a captured frame; specify glitter or suppression; associate the selection with its observation and scope; submit an objective. The interface need not interpret native rendering payloads.

properties.name: Activation · Review and enable policy
properties.description: Inspect the evaluated policy and its applicability, then request activation before runtime execution.

properties.name: Reference runtime restrictions
properties.description: These restrictions apply to the known reference transformation, not every future policy type.
statements: No two concurrent full renderings in production.
No mandatory CPU screenshot round trip.
No full-frame neural classification on every frame for the known resource substitution.
No continuous training or experimental capture in production runtime.

properties.name: Future experiment · Simulated phone feed
properties.description: Generate equivalent scrolling-feed states with advertisements present and absent or replaced. Capture available semantic, presentation-description and graphics representations. Test whether shared contracts remain unchanged; this is planned cross-domain validation, not demonstrated portability.

properties.name: A01 · Additional p99 critical-path cost
properties.description: At most 0.5 ms additional p99 critical-path frame cost on declared reference hardware and scene. Measure the combined transformed workload directly; baseline p99 plus overhead p99 does not prove transformed p99.

properties.name: A02 · Sustained 120 FPS
properties.description: At least 120 FPS when the fixed baseline workload has sufficient headroom. 120 FPS corresponds to approximately 8.33 ms per frame; no universal performance guarantee is implied.

properties.name: A03 · Baseline headroom
properties.description: Use a fixed workload with baseline p99 frame time no greater than 7.8 ms. This is workload qualification, not proof that adding the 0.5 ms target preserves all frame deadlines.

properties.name: A04 · Zero added queued frames
properties.description: No additional queued frames from runtime transformation; measure input-to-display latency separately.

properties.name: A05 · Off-path preparation
properties.description: Prepare runtime policies outside the frame-critical path.

properties.name: A06 · No required full-frame model
properties.description: Full-frame model execution is not required for the known resource-substitution policy.

properties.name: A07 · Zero prohibited presented occurrences
properties.description: Zero strictly prohibited presented occurrences in covered production scenarios. If pre-exposure prevention cannot be guaranteed, report unsupported or use an explicitly authorized conservative mode.

properties.name: A08 · Zero unauthorized negative-case changes
properties.description: Zero unauthorized changes in controlled negative cases. Shared-resource effects require specific targeting.

properties.name: A09 · Valid scope
properties.description: The policy applies only within evaluated applicability conditions and produces the specified change.

properties.name: A10 · Independent evidence
properties.description: Captured paired evidence includes attributable originating conditions, representations and observed outcomes that can be independently verified.

properties.name: A11 · Reproducible experiment
properties.description: Experimental outcomes reproduce within explicitly declared tolerances.

properties.name: A12 · Independent realization substitution
properties.description: At least two independently implemented bindings demonstrate the same relevant contract and invariant obligations without redefining meaning.

properties.name: Measurement protocol
properties.description: Acceptance targets require recorded measurement evidence. Verification state comes from assessments, not authored status labels.
statements: Pin reference hardware, driver, scene, workload and declared tolerances.
Disable capture, tracing and offline analysis during production performance measurements.
Measure frame presentation, GPU execution, CPU submission and input-to-display latency separately.
Record paired baseline and transformed workload results, including distributions and negative cases.
A known material replacement may require little recurring computation; an unseen semantic category may not.

properties.name: T01 · Shared resource
properties.description: Target effect shares a resource with desirable content; reject unsafe broad replacement.

properties.name: T02 · Shader identity changes
properties.description: Application update changes shader identity; do not silently reuse an invalid policy.

properties.name: T03 · Unavailable capability
properties.description: Policy references an unavailable capability; explicitly report unsupported.

properties.name: T04 · Dynamic resource recreation
properties.description: Resources are dynamically recreated; target tracking and installation must remain valid or fail observably.

properties.name: T05 · Unsupported graphics API
properties.description: Target uses an unsupported graphics API; do not claim compatibility.

properties.name: T06 · Unrelated changes
properties.description: Candidate changes unrelated objects; evaluation must reject unauthorized modification.

properties.name: T07 · Budget exceeded
properties.description: Intervention exceeds frame-time budget; report failed performance conformance.

properties.name: T08 · Protected rendering path
properties.description: Protected or inaccessible rendering prevents observation; report limitation without circumvention.

properties.name: E1 · Experimentation acceptance
properties.description: Controlled equivalent experiences yield alternative native renderings with preserved causal correspondence.

properties.name: E2 · Synthesis acceptance
properties.description: A policy is derived from evidence, evaluated against the objective, and published with applicability and capability requirements.

properties.name: E3 · Execution acceptance
properties.description: A supported binding modifies normal production behavior without continuous full-frame classification for the reference policy.

properties.name: E4 · Interaction acceptance
properties.description: A user expresses or corrects the transformation without knowing graphics implementation details.

properties.name: E5 · Substitution acceptance
properties.description: Two realization bindings demonstrate compliance with the same relevant domain meanings and system contracts.

properties.name: E6 · Performance acceptance
properties.description: The modified reference workload meets declared 120 FPS frame-time, presentation-latency and correctness requirements.

properties.name: 1 · Architectural foundation
properties.description: Exit: replace a system implementation without changing conceptual responsibility or contract semantics.
statements: Versioned domain ontology and system contracts.
Realization ontology, capabilities and binding validity rules.
Contract conformance tests; minimum evidence and policy definitions.

properties.name: 2 · Counterfactual experimentation
properties.description: Exit: S1 produces comparable causally attributed representations and verifies their presentations.
statements: Controlled game scene and reproducible inputs/state.
Original and transformed variants with native capture.
Paired correspondence evidence; replay and verification procedure.

properties.name: 3 · Policy synthesis
properties.description: Exit: S2 derives an executable policy from evidence and its observed effect is independently verified.
statements: Evidence consumption and replaceable synthesis.
Candidate generation and controlled evaluation using S1.
Versioned policy artifacts with validation evidence.

properties.name: 4 · Runtime mediation
properties.description: Exit: the reference game in its original configuration presents the transformed effect while satisfying correctness and performance targets.
statements: Capability discovery; preparation and installation.
Shader/resource-level intervention in a single normal production path.
Performance instrumentation and negative tests.

properties.name: 5 · Preference interaction
properties.description: Exit: a user identifies unwanted content, requests its replacement and experiences the evaluated transformation without manually editing graphics resources.
statements: Region selection and objective specification.
Policy association and activation.
Correction and feedback flow.

properties.name: 6 · Architectural substitution
properties.description: Exit: unchanged domain and system models operate through different realization technologies for the same relevant contract.
statements: Second independently implemented observation or intervention binding.
Conformance and capability compatibility tests.
Explicit supported and unsupported policy scope.

properties.name: 7 · Cross-domain validation
properties.description: Exit: the simulated phone-feed scenario needs new bindings/policies but no redefinition of shared ontologies; this remains a hypothesis to test.
statements: Equivalent scrolling-feed alternatives with ads present and absent or replaced.
Capture at available semantic, presentation-description and graphics boundaries.
Evaluate shared contracts without changing their meaning.

properties.name: Binding validity
properties.description: A binding is valid only when its capabilities fulfill the assigned contract, execution preserves applicable invariants, limitations are explicit and performance is evaluated against declared constraints.
statements: One binding may use several boundaries.
One technology may realize several systems.
Different technologies may satisfy the same contract without sharing native representations.
An attempts_to_fulfill relation is an obligation, not a proof of satisfaction.

properties.name: Independent meanings and responsibilities
properties.description: Domain defines meaning; systems own responsibilities; realizations provide mechanisms.
statements: Changing engine, graphics API or operating system must not redefine domain concepts or the four responsibilities.
Local system vocabularies reference canonical concepts, specializing only when additional semantics exist.
Capability is defined once; architectural Binding and runtime Policy Binding have distinct meanings.

properties.name: Boundary contracts and native representations
properties.description: Standardize meaning at system boundaries without unnecessarily converting native payloads into a universal representation.
statements: Version system contracts and keep core contracts language-agnostic.
Keep native payloads accessible and explicitly typed; large binary observations may live separately from metadata.
C1–C5 specify information exchanged, whereas behavioral contracts specify system obligations.

properties.name: Implementation constraints
properties.description: Experimental machinery must remain separate from production execution.
statements: Experimental capture is not required in production runtime.
Prepare policies before activation wherever possible.
Published executable policies include evidence of validity and supported scope.
Personal screen captures and preference data remain local by default.

properties.name: Project-specific work and reuse
properties.description: Build only the semantics and coordination not provided by existing capabilities.
statements: Project-specific: counterfactual evidence semantics, system contracts and binding validity.
Project-specific: policy-synthesis orchestration and preference semantics.
Reuse simulation, graphics APIs/drivers, capture/replay, inspection, shader tooling and compatible learning infrastructure.
Reference documentation categories: Godot rendering architecture, Vulkan Layers, GFXReconstruct, RenderDoc, Mesa SPIR-V replacement and Vulkan profiling. Candidate suitability remains unevaluated.

properties.name: Questions for a new environment
properties.description: Investigate capability sufficiency before choosing a realization.
statements: What information does this environment expose?
What can be changed at each boundary?
Can those capabilities satisfy an existing system contract?
Does the intervention preserve correctness and performance?

properties.name: What the MCP can establish
properties.description: The MCP enforces registered types, legal endpoints, cardinality, required references, uniqueness and evidence structure. It cannot establish causal equivalence, semantic preservation or measured performance from assertions alone.
statements: Structural validation alone cannot establish binding conformance.
Assessment completion is not proof; a passing result requires declared evidence obligations, whose truth still needs independent evaluation.
Changes invalidate dependent assessments; explicit unsupported states must not be replaced with weaker promises.

properties.name: Semantic recognition from composed pixels
properties.description: Infer the intended target from composed pixels with sufficient specificity; intrinsic object identity is not assumed. Recognition must satisfy the objective's preservation, latency and exposure constraints.

properties.name: S3 · Engine-level intervention binding
properties.description: May modify identified materials or effects before rendering. Validity depends on demonstrated semantic targeting, preservation and performance through available engine controls.

properties.name: S3 · Compositor intervention binding
properties.description: May modify composed pixels, but has no intrinsic blood-object identity. Additional recognition is required, and latency, preservation and exposure obligations still apply.

properties.name: One objective and contract, three candidate realizations
properties.description: The engine, graphics-API and compositor candidates attempt the same S3 contract. Their available information, control and costs differ; substitutability requires evidence that the unchanged objective, contract and applicable invariants remain satisfied.
